**Diede de Groot** (pronounced [[ˈdidə də ˈɣroːt]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Dutch "Help:IPA/Dutch") [](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/f/f8/Nl-de_Groot.ogg/Nl-de_Groot.ogg.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nl-de_Groot.ogg "File:Nl-de Groot.ogg")[wheelchair tennis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wheelchair_tennis "Wheelchair tennis") player who was world No. 1 in both singles and doubles.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diede_de_Groot#cite_note-1)
De Groot is a 43–time [major](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Slam_\(tennis\)#Tournaments "Grand Slam \(tennis\)") champion, having won a record 24 titles in singles and 19 in doubles. De Groot had a three-year, 145-match, winning streak in singles, from a defeat in February 2021 to [Yui Kamiji](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yui_Kamiji "Yui Kamiji") until a defeat in May 2024 to [Li Xiaohui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Li_Xiaohui_\(tennis\) "Li Xiaohui \(tennis\)").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diede_de_Groot#cite_note-100_match_wins-2) During this streak she achieved the first calendar-year [Super Slam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Slam_\(tennis\)#Super_Slam "Grand Slam \(tennis\)") in tennis history by winning all four major titles, the [Paralympic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_Paralympic_Games "Summer Paralympic Games") gold medal, and the [Wheelchair Tennis Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wheelchair_Tennis_Masters "Wheelchair Tennis Masters") title in women's singles in 2021.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diede_de_Groot#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diede_de_Groot#cite_note-SuperSlam-4) The following year, she became the first player in any discipline of tennis to defend the [Grand Slam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Slam_\(tennis\) "Grand Slam \(tennis\)") and win all four majors in two consecutive years, and did so yet again in 2023.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diede_de_Groot#cite_note-5) At the [2026 French Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_French_Open_%E2%80%93_Wheelchair_women's_singles "2026 French Open – Wheelchair women's singles"), she became the first player ever to achieve the [sextuple career Grand Slam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Slam_\(tennis\)#Career_Grand_Slam "Grand Slam \(tennis\)").
In doubles, de Groot completed the Grand Slam in 2019, partnering [Aniek van Koot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aniek_van_Koot "Aniek van Koot"). Apart from her major titles, de Groot has won multiple Wheelchair Tennis Masters titles between 2016 and 2018 in both singles and doubles, as well as gold medals in both disciplines at the [2020 Tokyo Paralympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wheelchair_tennis_at_the_2020_Summer_Paralympics "Wheelchair tennis at the 2020 Summer Paralympics").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diede_de_Groot#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diede_de_Groot#cite_note-7) She was part of the Dutch team that won the World Team Cup on eight occasions between 2011 and 2019.
## Career
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Diede_de_Groot&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Career")]
### Early years
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Diede_de_Groot&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early years")]
De Groot was born with [unequal leg length](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unequal_leg_length "Unequal leg length") and began her wheelchair tennis career at age seven.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diede_de_Groot#cite_note-8) She started playing on the [ITF Wheelchair Tennis Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITF_Wheelchair_Tennis_Tour "ITF Wheelchair Tennis Tour") in 2009 as a junior player.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diede_de_Groot#cite_note-itf-9) During her time with the ITF, De Groot won the Cruyff Foundation Junior Masters in 2013 in singles and doubles. The following year, she won the 2014 Junior Masters in doubles.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diede_de_Groot#cite_note-paralympics-10)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9b/Diede_de_Groot_tennis_player_2014.jpg/250px-Diede_de_Groot_tennis_player_2014.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Diede_de_Groot_tennis_player_2014.jpg) De Groot in 2014
De Groot competed at the [2016 Summer Paralympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Paralympics "2016 Summer Paralympics") in singles and doubles competitions. While De Groot did not medal in singles, she won a silver medal in women's doubles.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diede_de_Groot#cite_note-paralympics-10)
She has also appeared at the [BNP Paribas World Team Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BNP_Paribas_World_Team_Cup?action=edit&redlink=1 "BNP Paribas World Team Cup \(page does not exist\)") in consecutive years from 2011 to 2019. At the World Team Cup, De Groot started as a junior in 2011 before competing a world team competitor in 2012.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diede_de_Groot#cite_note-itf-9)
### 2017–2019: First Grand Slam appearances and titles
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Diede_de_Groot&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2017–2019: First Grand Slam appearances and titles")]
De Groot made her first [Grand Slam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Slam_\(tennis\) "Grand Slam \(tennis\)") appearance at the [2017 Australian Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Australian_Open "2017 Australian Open").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diede_de_Groot#cite_note-11) After placing in the quarterfinals at the Australian Open and the [2017 French Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_French_Open "2017 French Open"), de Groot won her first Grand Slam title at the [2017 Wimbledon Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Wimbledon_Championships "2017 Wimbledon Championships"). She ended the 2017 Grand Slam tournaments with a finals finish at the [2017 US Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_US_Open_\(tennis\) "2017 US Open \(tennis\)").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diede_de_Groot#cite_note-ausopen-12) At the start of 2018, she won the [2018 Australian Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Australian_Open "2018 Australian Open") and appeared at the final of the [2018 French Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_French_Open "2018 French Open").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diede_de_Groot#cite_note-13) For the remaining Grand Slams of 2018, De Groot won the women's singles division at the [2018 Wimbledon Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_Wimbledon_Championships "2018 Wimbledon Championships") and her first US Open singles title at the [2018 US Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_US_Open_\(tennis\) "2018 US Open \(tennis\)").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diede_de_Groot#cite_note-Stevenson-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diede_de_Groot#cite_note-15) In 2019, de Groot rewon the Australian Open title in singles competition at the [2019 Australian Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Australian_Open "2019 Australian Open").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diede_de_Groot#cite_note-16) At the [2019 French Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_French_Open "2019 French Open"), de Groot completed her career Grand Slam when she won her first French Open singles title.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diede_de_Groot#cite_note-17) Her French Open title also made de Groot the first wheelchair tennis player to complete a [Non-calendar year Grand Slam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Slam_\(tennis\)#Non-calendar-year_Grand_Slam "Grand Slam \(tennis\)") (win all four Grand Slam singles events in a row, but not in the same year).[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diede_de_Groot#cite_note-ipc2019-18) At the [2019 Wimbledon Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Wimbledon_Championships "2019 Wimbledon Championships"), de Groot ended her back to back singles wins when she was defeated by [Aniek van Koot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aniek_van_Koot "Aniek van Koot") in the final.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diede_de_Groot#cite_note-19) In 2021, she won the Wimbledon Single Ladies Wheelchair championship.
In doubles, De Groot was a runner up in the 2017 Australian, French and Wimbledon championships.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diede_de_Groot#cite_note-ausopen-12) After winning her first doubles title at the 2017 US Open, she lost at the 2018 Australian Open and co-won the doubles event at the 2018 French Open.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diede_de_Groot#cite_note-20) De Groot became the first woman in wheelchair tennis to win both the women's singles and doubles events at Wimbledon in July 2018.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diede_de_Groot#cite_note-Stevenson-14) She won her second US Open doubles title at the 2018 US Open alongside [Yui Kamiji](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yui_Kamiji "Yui Kamiji").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diede_de_Groot#cite_note-21) At the 2019 Australian Open, De Groot won her first Australian doubles title with [Aniek van Koot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aniek_van_Koot "Aniek van Koot") alongside her singles title in January 2019.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diede_de_Groot#cite_note-22) At the following Grand Slams, De Groot and Van Koot won the 2019 doubles titles at the French Open and Wimbledon.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diede_de_Groot#cite_note-ipc2019-18)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diede_de_Groot#cite_note-23)
In Masters competitions, De Groot won the 2017 and 2018 [Wheelchair Tennis Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wheelchair_Tennis_Masters "Wheelchair Tennis Masters") in women's singles.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diede_de_Groot#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diede_de_Groot#cite_note-25) Competing in doubles, she won the [2016 Wheelchair Doubles Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Wheelchair_Doubles_Masters "2016 Wheelchair Doubles Masters") with [Lucy Shuker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucy_Shuker "Lucy Shuker") and the [2017 Wheelchair Doubles Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Wheelchair_Doubles_Masters "2017 Wheelchair Doubles Masters") alongside [Marjolein Buis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marjolein_Buis "Marjolein Buis").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diede_de_Groot#cite_note-26)
### 2021: Paralympics gold medals and calendar year Super Slam
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Diede_de_Groot&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2021: Paralympics gold medals and calendar year Super Slam")]
In 2021, De Groot earned the calendar year Super Slam, winning singles titles in the [Australian Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Open "Australian Open"), [French Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Open "French Open"), [Wimbledon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Championships,_Wimbledon "The Championships, Wimbledon"), [US Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Open_\(tennis\) "US Open \(tennis\)"), the singles gold medal at the [2020 Summer Paralympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Summer_Paralympics "2020 Summer Paralympics") and the singles titles in the [Wheelchair Tennis Masters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wheelchair_Tennis_Masters "Wheelchair Tennis Masters").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diede_de_Groot#cite_note-SuperSlam-4) She was the first professional wheelchair tennis player to achieve the feat in the history of the sport.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diede_de_Groot#cite_note-SuperSlam-4)
De Groot also competed at the [2020 Summer Paralympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Summer_Paralympics "2020 Summer Paralympics"), winning gold medals in both singles and doubles.
### 2022
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Diede_de_Groot&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2022")]
In June, De Groot won the inaugural women's wheelchair singles title at the [Eastbourne International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastbourne_International "Eastbourne International"), an ITF 2 grass-court event, defeating [Cornelia Oosthuizen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornelia_Oosthuizen "Cornelia Oosthuizen") in the first round and [Kgothatso Montjane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kgothatso_Montjane "Kgothatso Montjane") in the semifinals before overcoming Yui Kamiji 6–3, 6–2 in the final. The victory marked her sixth singles title of the 2022 season and extended her winning streak to 52 matches.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diede_de_Groot#cite_note-de_groot_eastbourne_title_2026-27)

### 2024: Sixth Australian Open singles title and more Paralympic medals
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Diede_de_Groot&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2024: Sixth Australian Open singles title and more Paralympic medals")]
De Groot won her sixth Australian singles title at the [2024 Australian Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Australian_Open "2024 Australian Open"), defeating Kamiji in the final in straight sets. It was her 21st singles title at a Grand Slam tournament, equaling a record set by compatriot [Esther Vergeer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esther_Vergeer "Esther Vergeer").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diede_de_Groot#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diede_de_Groot#cite_note-30)
De Groot won silver medals in both women's [singles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wheelchair_tennis_at_the_2024_Summer_Paralympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_singles "Wheelchair tennis at the 2024 Summer Paralympics – Women's singles")[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diede_de_Groot#cite_note-kamiji_paralympic_gold_2024-31) and [doubles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wheelchair_tennis_at_the_2024_Summer_Paralympics_%E2%80%93_Women's_doubles "Wheelchair tennis at the 2024 Summer Paralympics – Women's doubles"), partnering with [Aniek van Koot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aniek_van_Koot "Aniek van Koot"),[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diede_de_Groot#cite_note-paris2024_day8_medal_moments-32) at the [2024 Summer Paralympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Paralympics "2024 Summer Paralympics").

### 2026: Sixth French Open singles title and sixth career grand slam, Australian Open and Wimbledon runner up
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Diede_de_Groot&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 2026: Sixth French Open singles title and sixth career grand slam, Australian Open and Wimbledon runner up")]
Playing at the [2026 Australian Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Australian_Open "2026 Australian Open"), de Groot was runner up at the singles tournament, being defeated in two sets by Chinese [Li Xiaohui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Li_Xiaohui_\(tennis\) "Li Xiaohui \(tennis\)") at the final.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diede_de_Groot#cite_note-33)
At the [2026 French Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_French_Open "2026 French Open"), de Groot won her sixth title on wheelchair women's singles after defeating [Ksenia Chasteau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ksenia_Chasteau "Ksenia Chasteau") in two sets at the final, which also marked the sixth time she achieved the singles career slam.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diede_de_Groot#cite_note-rg_live_june6_2026-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diede_de_Groot#cite_note-oda_degroot_vink_rg2026-35)
